name: thin-results
about: Results exist but each rests on one or two leads: too thin to steer by.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: A small fleet where dispatch knows your name

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.
Our ads with hook straight_talk (straight talk) and scene cab_pov (from the cab) spent $41.20 in the last 28 days over 3010 impressions and brought 1 lead, $41.20 per lead.
Our ads with hook proof (proof) and scene equipment_at_rest (truck at rest) spent $38.75 in the last 28 days over 2890 impressions and brought 2 leads, $19.38 per lead.

output.audience: Class A drivers who already pull flatbed and meet the experience requirement, living on or near the Midwest lanes. They likely run for a larger fleet now, out longer or in a shared truck. Home weekly, an assigned truck and a dispatcher who knows their name would make them stop.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile for flatbed work on Midwest lanes, shown over a loaded flatbed moving on the road.
angles.proof: The job states the pay per mile and that the work is flatbed on Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Pay per mile is the most concrete fact on the job and flatbed drivers compare it quickly. Nothing has been measured for this hook and scene yet.

angles.idea: Lead with getting home weekly, pictured as the driver's own street at the end of a regional run.
angles.proof: The job offers home weekly on a regional Class A route.
angles.why: Home weekly is what separates this regional job from longer-haul work. This hook and scene have no history here, so it is a test.

angles.idea: Lead with the assigned truck: the same flatbed tractor waiting for the same driver, shown parked and ready.
angles.proof: The job lists an assigned truck and flatbed equipment.
angles.why: An assigned truck is a fact a small fleet can show plainly. Earlier ads with a truck-at-rest picture had the lower cost per lead, but over very few leads, so that is thin.

angles.idea: Say plainly who this is for: Class A with the stated experience, Midwest lanes, a small fleet where dispatch knows your name.
angles.proof: The job states the experience requirement and Midwest lanes, and describes a small fleet where dispatch knows your name.
angles.why: Stating the requirement and the area up front screens out drivers who do not fit. The earlier ads of this kind brought too few leads to judge, so this is a retry with plainer facts.

angles.idea: Set the job's facts side by side on a plain plate: the pay per mile, home weekly and the retirement plan.
angles.proof: The job states the pay per mile, home weekly and a retirement plan.
angles.why: The earlier proof ads had the lower cost per lead, though over very few leads, so this is thin. A plain plate lets the job's facts carry the ad.
